analysis.investment_thesis: Fedbank Financial Services is a growing NBFC with Federal Bank parentage and reasonable loan book expansion, but an 8.84% ROE — well below my 15% floor — combined with declining FY2025 profits signals poor capital efficiency. The structural leverage of 3.83x D/E is unavoidable in lending, but this business is not yet earning a satisfactory return on the equity it holds.
key_strengths: Federal Bank promoter holding at 60.79% — stable, regulated parent with institutional credibility
Strong revenue CAGR of 32.2% (FY2022–25), indicating real loan book demand in gold, housing, and SME segments
Collateral-backed lending mix (gold loans, LAP, home equity) provides downside protection on asset quality
key_risks: ROE of 8.84% is far below my 15% minimum — this business is not compounding equity at an acceptable rate
Profits actually declined in FY2025 (₹225 Cr vs ₹245 Cr in FY2024) — a trend reversal after three years of growth is a serious warning sign
Total debt doubled from ₹5,154 Cr to ₹10,437 Cr in three years; aggressive AUM expansion funded entirely by borrowed capital leaves no margin for a credit cycle downturn
red_flags: Net profit and EBITDA both fell in FY2025 — margin compression at the same time the loan book is expanding suggests rising credit costs or funding cost pressure
Operating cash flow negative all four years (₹-578 Cr to ₹-978 Cr) — while structurally normal for NBFCs, the worsening trend is not comforting
Forward P/E of 11.35x implies a sharp earnings recovery priced in; if FY2026 disappoints, there is meaningful downside at current price
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my perspective, Fedbank Financial Services fails the most fundamental test: the business is not earning a satisfactory return on shareholders' equity. An ROE of 8.84% means for every ₹100 of equity I put in, the company is earning less than ₹9 per year. That is unacceptable. I built DMart to earn 18-22% on every rupee of capital. An NBFC operating with 3.83x leverage — meaning the loan book is amplified many times over equity — should be generating ROE of at least 15-18% to justify the risk. Fedbank is not delivering that. The profit decline in FY2025 (from ₹245 Cr to ₹225 Cr) while revenues still grew 30% tells me that asset quality, funding costs, or provisioning is deteriorating quietly beneath the surface of impressive top-line growth.

The Federal Bank parentage is a genuine comfort for governance and access to capital — the promoter holding is stable at 60.79% and the parent has regulatory credibility. The loan mix is also sensible: gold loans, housing, and LAP are collateral-backed businesses I respect. But a good parent and a sensible product mix cannot compensate for a business that is expanding its balance sheet (total assets grew from ₹6,556 Cr to ₹13,250 Cr in three years) while simultaneously seeing its profitability plateau and contract. This is the opposite of what I look for — I want businesses where unit economics improve as they scale. At a P/E of 17.5x with declining earnings, the valuation is not cheap enough to offset the quality concerns. I would wait for ROE to durably cross 14-15% and profits to resume a clear upward trajectory before reconsidering.
